RecordMicDataClip.blurb: Console function: record raw + processed mic for MicData_ClipRecordTime_ms.

MicData_CollectRawTriggers.blurb: When true, each wake-word hit also saves the unprocessed four-channel mic audio for that short “trigger only” clip (not just the combined mono). Off by default so only the processed single-channel trigger WAV is written.
MicData_CollectRawTriggers.detail: On non-shipping (ANKI_DEV_CHEATS) builds, every recognized wake word already creates a short capture job under triggersOnly/ that always records processed (beamformed/combined) audio plus ~170 ms after the trigger ends. Turning this on also enables MicDataType::Raw for that same job: four raw mic channels interlaced into a *_raw.wav next to the processed .wav. Caps at 100 files per folder (oldest overwritten). Shipping builds without cheats do not create trigger-only jobs, so this has no effect there.
MicData_CollectRawTriggers.howTo: 1) Use a build with ANKI_DEV_CHEATS. 2) Set true. 3) Say the wake word. 4) Pull files from the robot cache (see paths).

paths.notes: HTTP browse: http://ROBOT_IP:8889/cache/micdata/triggersOnly/. Files look like miccapture_*/*.wav and *_raw.wav. Scripts: tools/ear_puller.py, project/victor/scripts/pull_micdata.sh.

MicData_CollectRawTriggers.statusNote: Only affects captures created under ANKI_DEV_CHEATS (trigger-only jobs). Registration is not cheats-gated, but the save path is.

MicData_ForceDisableMicDataProc.blurb: When true (and ForceEnable is off), forces the voice-activity flag off so the wake-word recognizer is told “no activity” and can skip trigger recognition for that audio block. Default false. Does not stop raw mic hardware or Signal Essence beamforming — it only gates the activity flag used for recognition.
MicData_ForceDisableMicDataProc.detail: Under ANKI_DEV_CHEATS only. After VAD / quiet-time / robot-noise logic sets activityFlag, these force vars override it: if ForceEnable is true, activity is forced on; else if ForceDisable is true, activity is forced off (mutual exclusion: Enable wins). ProcessTriggerLoop passes (activeState != 0) into SpeechRecognizerSystem::Update — false means skip RecognizeTriggerWord work for that block. Default ForceEnable is true, so Disable does nothing until you turn ForceEnable off first.
MicData_ForceDisableMicDataProc.howTo: 1) Set MicData_ForceEnableMicDataProc to false. 2) Set MicData_ForceDisableMicDataProc to true. 3) Confirm wake-word recognition no longer runs (CPU / logs).
MicData_ForceDisableMicDataProc.statusNote: ANKI_DEV_CHEATS only. Ineffective while ForceEnable remains at default true (if/else priority).

MicData_ForceEnableMicDataProc.blurb: When true (the default on cheats builds), always marks mic audio as “active” so wake-word recognition never skips a block for silence. When false, normal VAD + quiet-time + robot-noise activity logic applies (unless ForceDisable is on).
MicData_ForceEnableMicDataProc.detail: Under ANKI_DEV_CHEATS only. Overrides activityFlag after VAD: ForceEnable → activityFlag=1; else ForceDisable → 0. Default true means the quiet-time skip path is effectively bypassed for recognition — useful so motor/speaker/VAD edge cases do not drop “Hey Vector,” at the cost of always running the recognizer. Mutual exclusion with ForceDisable: if both are true, Enable wins (if/else).
MicData_ForceEnableMicDataProc.howTo: Leave true for max wake-word reliability in tests. Set false to restore VAD-gated recognition (then optionally enable ForceDisable to force all-off).
MicData_ForceEnableMicDataProc.statusNote: ANKI_DEV_CHEATS only. Default true already forces activity on every block.

MicData_QuietTimeCooldown_ms.blurb: How long (ms) voice activity must stay quiet before the system stops treating audio as “active” and can skip wake-word recognition for silence. Default 1000 ms; console range 500–10000. Comment in code: keep at least as long as the wake-word phrase (~500–750 ms).
MicData_QuietTimeCooldown_ms.detail: Each 10 ms mic chunk runs a simple VAD (DoSVad). On any activity (including forced activity from motors or speaker noise), a countdown is reset to QuietTimeCooldown_ms / chunk length. While the countdown is non-zero, activityFlag stays 1 even if VAD itself is quiet — so the end of “Hey Vector” is not cut off by a brief dip in energy. When countdown hits 0, activityFlag can be 0 and ProcessTriggerLoop skips recognizer work for that block. Overridden afterward if ForceEnable (always on) or ForceDisable (always off) applies under cheats.
MicData_QuietTimeCooldown_ms.statusNote: On typical cheats builds ForceEnable defaults true, so this cooldown has little practical effect until ForceEnable is turned off.

MicData_SaveRawFullIntent.blurb: When true, wake-word streaming also saves the full four-channel raw mic capture for the post-trigger intent stream (not only the processed mono WAV). Off by default. Applies to normal wake-word streams only — not blackjack/knowledge-graph wake-wordless streams.
MicData_SaveRawFullIntent.detail: CreateStreamJob for CloudMic::StreamType::Normal (after wake word) always enables processed file collect under ANKI_DEV_CHEATS. This flag additionally EnableDataCollect(Raw). Files go under triggeredCapture/, up to 100 entries. Raw is interlaced 4-channel *_raw.wav; processed is mono .wav. Wake-wordless intents use MicData_SaveRawFullIntent_WakeWordless instead.
MicData_SaveRawFullIntent.howTo: 1) Set true on anim console. 2) Trigger a normal “Hey Vector” stream. 3) Pull /cache/micdata/triggeredCapture/.

paths.notes: HTTP: http://ROBOT_IP:8889/cache/micdata/triggeredCapture/. Pair with MicData_CollectRawTriggers for short wake-word-only raw clips under triggersOnly/.

MicData_SaveRawFullIntent.statusNote: Registration and use are under ANKI_DEV_CHEATS only.

MicData_SaveRawFullIntent_WakeWordless.blurb: Same as SaveRawFullIntent, but for wake-wordless cloud streams (Blackjack and Knowledge Graph stream types) instead of the normal “Hey Vector then talk” path. When true, those streams also write four-channel raw audio under triggeredCapture/.
MicData_SaveRawFullIntent_WakeWordless.detail: CreateStreamJob switches on stream type: Normal → MicData_SaveRawFullIntent; Blackjack / KnowledgeGraph → this flag. Engine/cloud can start wake-wordless streaming via MicDataSystem::StartWakeWordlessStreaming, which calls CreateStreamJob with that type after earcon timing. Processed capture still defaults on under ANKI_DEV_CHEATS; this only adds raw. Same folder/cap as normal triggeredCapture jobs.
MicData_SaveRawFullIntent_WakeWordless.howTo: 1) Set true. 2) Trigger a knowledge-graph / blackjack (wake-wordless) stream from the product path. 3) Inspect triggeredCapture/ for *_raw.wav.

paths.notes: Same directory as normal intent captures; distinguish by when you triggered the stream. HTTP: http://ROBOT_IP:8889/cache/micdata/triggeredCapture/.

MicData_SaveRawFullIntent_WakeWordless.statusNote: Registration and use under ANKI_DEV_CHEATS. Only affects Blackjack/KnowledgeGraph stream types.

MicData_SpeakerNoiseDisablesMics.blurb: When true (default), treat “speaker is playing robot audio” like motor noise: force voice-activity on, turn Signal Essence beamforming off, and clear mic direction estimates so Vector does not trust a DOA while the speaker is loud. When false, only physical robot motion counts as that noise; speaker playback alone does not disable beamforming/direction.
MicData_SpeakerNoiseDisablesMics.detail: hasRobotNoise = robotIsMoving OR (speakerActive AND this flag). Speaker active includes a short cooldown after playback stops (speaker latency). Effects of hasRobotNoise: (1) VAD activity forced true so wake-word work is not skipped during robot sound; (2) processing state set to SigEsBeamformingOff when not in low-power; (3) winning/selected mic direction forced to “unknown.” Name says “disables mics” but hardware stays up — it disables beamforming/DOA trust and assumes activity while the speaker is noisy.
